assign.request: Day page UX: one scroll region (fix the two scrollbars at the cause), strip → clickable now-first overview (active with now+steps, landed rows with outcome headline + pills, rest folded, day.jsonl a click), overview→drill-down; ux-v1 prompt run before and after

log.msg: skill: layout. ux-v1 written (30 lines: purpose / most-important-first / missing / glance-click-scroll / affordance / scroll regions, then the usual JSON block) and run on /framework/ai/2026-08-17/ at 900,1440,3440 --regions none, sonnet, 3 shots $0.23. All three answers agree: the eye lands on the giant date, the twelve grey day.jsonl lines read AS the task list and are the top 'broken' finding at 1440 and 3440 -- 'no link affordance despite almost certainly being clickable task links' -- and ACTIVE is below them (at 3440 it is at the very bottom of the first screen). Two flagged the date heading as eating a quarter of the viewport.

PURPOSE (mine): the day page answers 'what is running right now, and what landed today' -- every task of the day as a clickable row, active first. It is not a log to read; it is a switchboard to click.

WHAT MIKE MIGHT WANT, ranked: 1 what is running now (name, now-line, step bar, since when, quiet?); 2 a click into any task; 3 what landed today, one headline each + its deliverable links; 4 today's spend and pace; 5 the counts (N running / N landed / N proposed); 6 what is proposed but unstarted; 7 the screenshots/deliverables without opening the task; 8 the raw day.jsonl timeline, on demand.

GLANCE: the group counts, the active cards with now+step bar, the first landed headlines. CLICK: a task name -> its page; a links pill -> the deliverable; an effort tag -> the effort board; 'timeline' -> day.jsonl. SCROLL: the rest of the landed run, then proposed. Nothing on the page should be prose you cannot click or a number you cannot act on.

TWO SCROLLBARS, cause found and measured @1440. Page.css:20 .pages{overflow-y:scroll} always reserves the sheet's gutter -- right on a normal page, where .pages IS the scroller (/framework/styles/ 900/4971, /framework/ai/ 900/25782). On a routed catalog page catalog.css:47 caps the page (overflow:hidden; grid-template-rows:minmax(0,1fr)) and catalog.css:119 makes .page-catalog-pages the scrollport instead: measured /framework/ai/2026-08-17/ = .pages 900/900 (dead reserved bar) + .page-catalog-pages 900/9640 (live inset bar). Two bars, one of them dead. Not Page.css's fault and not catalog.css's: the day page is only inside a catalog because ai/page.js calls catalog(), and ai.css:230 already hides the rail the moment a day or task is routed -- so the split is a wrapper with one region and no rail. Fix goes in ai.css, the file that already owns both :has() arrangement rules.

ONE SCROLL REGION landed, in ai.css only -- Page.css and catalog.css untouched. One nested block, scoped by '> .ai-index-rail' so no other catalog on the site is touched: release catalog.css's ceiling (overflow:visible; grid-template-rows:none) when a day or task is routed, because the rule above it has already hidden the rail and a split with one region is not a split. Two traps hit and both are in the comment: (1) as a flat second rule the .page-catalog-pages half read (0,6,0) and LOST to catalog.css's (0,8,0) -- nesting it inside the parent gives it (0,10,0); (2) with the ceiling gone, 'overflow-y:auto' on a flex item is an automatic minimum size of ZERO, and below 64em catalog.css turns the row into a COLUMN where 'flex:1 1 0' is a height basis of zero -- the day page rendered 622x0 and BLANK at 900 while fine at 1440. Both fixed (overflow-y:visible; flex:1 1 auto). Measured 1440: before .pages 900/900 dead + .page-catalog-pages 900/9640 live; after .pages 900/5602 and no inner scrollport at 900, 1440 or 3440. Every other page on the site scrolls in .pages -- the day page now does too.

DELETED (each one failed 'is it a link or a number?'): the 12-line day.jsonl header strip (700px, every line naming a task, none of them a link) -- it is a fold at the FOOT now, on 'wide', 111 lines, every one an <a> to its task; card.js's t.m.tab, the VS Code window title on all 30 cards; a running card's dispatch 'request' (2 clamped lines of launch prompt above the step bar that already says what is happening -- 52px x 4 live tasks, and the single reason LANDED sat below the fold); two of the three lines of intro prose on 2026-08-17/page.js; ai.css's '.page > .ai-dashboard { grid-column: wide }' (dashboard.js says 'wide' itself now -- the fourth and last copy of the bleed payback rule, retired as its own comment asked). Also: Landed is a compact group (--clamp:1), Proposed is a fold, .ai-card drops the theme's 1.8 prose leading to 1.4, and the date h1 is 1.4em not 3em.

FIRST SCREEN @1440 after (900px tall, dev rail shut): date 2026-08-17 (y10) - 'Today, ranked ->' link (y67) - ACTIVE 4 (y124) - four running cards each with step bar, step, now line, effort tag and links pills, every title an <a> (y145-680) - LANDED 52 (y703) - wall-polish and ui-wall landed rows in full (y715-900). Before, the same 900px held: the date, three lines of intro prose, and twelve grey non-clickable log lines. Zero cards. At 3440: ACTIVE 4 plus twelve landed rows above the fold. Verified: both folds shut by default, 111 timeline lines all <a>, clicking one routes to /framework/ai/2026-08-17/wall-polish/, zero console errors.

ADDENDUM (e) THE ZERO TOP SPACE -- cause: public/styles.css:97, '.page.topic { --measure: 40em; --page-pad: 0; background: none; }'. --page-pad INHERITS (core/Page/Page.css says so in its own comment), so the framework SHELL's own opt-out was handed down to every .page nested inside it, and Page.css's 'padding: var(--page-pad, var(--pad-y) 0)' resolved to 0 for every page under /framework/ -- --pad-y:3em never fired once, sitewide. It was not the AI page. One-line fix, proven by injection before editing and then applied: '.page.topic { --measure: 40em; padding: 0; background: none; }' -- the shell opts ITSELF out and leaves the token alone. Measured @1440: /framework/ai/2026-08-17/ and /framework/styles/ both 0px -> 45.84px padding-top, first element y=0 -> y=92 / y=46; /framework/core/Page/ unchanged (Doc.css declares its own). SITEWIDE: every /framework/ page just gained ~46px top and bottom -- concurrent measuring agents' baselines moved. Twelve model reads never flagged it: a heading flush to the top edge reads as 'already scrolled'.

ADDENDUM (a)(b) card-fields.md written: every field a card can show, its range and what it links to, in three tables (who|what|figures) plus what is deliberately NOT rendered. prompts/card-ux-v1.md written from it (35 lines) and run --regions auto --max-regions 2 at 900,1440, sonnet, 6 shots $0.45 -> cards/vision.jsonl. Region picker spent 2 of 4 region shots on div.sidebar (it outranks a card on framed+area) -- worth a --sel flag on run.mjs, logged as a finding, not fixed here. Verdict, identical from the whole page @900 and from one cropped .ai-card @900: 'the pill-outlined effort tags read as the interactive elements while the actual primary entry point reads as inert label text' -- the task NAME had no link treatment. Also asked for, twice: elapsed time instead of a clock ('running since 4:40 PM' forces mental subtraction). Both fixed: .ai-card-title is var(--prim) not color:inherit, status() says 'running 1h 43m'. Third finding, the .ai-fold-bar reading as a caption, fixed with a disclosure triangle. Not fixed (not the card's): a task whose own steps[] entries carry semicolons renders a step line that looks like three concatenated steps.

ADDENDUM (c) LINKAGE, first 6 cards @1440, every href clicked or fetched: 33 links, 32 OK, 1 bad. 6 titles -> /framework/ai/2026-08-17/<slug>/ 200, h1 = the slug, all 6 correct. 6 effort tags -> /framework/ai/effort/{layout,ai-log,ai-ops,vision,web-ui,web-ui}/ 200, h1 = the effort name, all correct. 21 pills: 11 -> sibling task pages 200; 6 -> live site pages (/framework/ui/, /framework/styles/layouts/, /framework/ui/{tooltip,menu,crumbs,pagination}/, /framework/ext/catalog/) 200 with the right h1; 2 -> .md files 200 text/markdown; 1 -> /framework/ext/DesignTool/vision/ 200. THE ONE BAD: /framework/ext/DesignTool/vision/?run=/framework/ai/2026-08-17/vision-pilot/ returns 200 and renders the Vision browse page but the app also emits '404 - nothing matches' -- a ?run= deep link whose run dir no longer resolves. It is vision-pilot's own link, not a card defect; flagged for that task.

ADDENDUM (d) THE 2-COLUMN CARD-AS-NAV STATE DOES NOT EXIST. Shot /framework/ai/2026-08-17/ai-board-fix/ at 1440 and 3440 (task-1440.png, task-3440.png): .ai-index-rail computes display:none and .page-catalog has exactly ONE visible column (page-catalog-pages, 1111px at 1440, 2986px at 3440). That is ai-board-fix's deliberate rule from 90 minutes ago -- a routed task does not want the whole archive beside it. So there is nothing to judge as nav, and the honest report is that the arrangement was removed on purpose. One real cost measured while looking: the hidden rail still BUILDS 158 .ai-card elements on every day and task page before CSS hides them. That is dashboard.js rail()/all_tasks() work nobody sees -- a candidate for the next pass, not this fence.

assign.outcome:
**The day page is a switchboard, not a log.** At 1440 the first screen was the date, three lines of prose, and twelve grey non-clickable log lines — zero cards. It is now `ACTIVE 4` (four running tasks with step bars, `now` lines, effort tags and deliverable pills), `LANDED 52`, and the first landed rows. Every task name is a link; 33 links across the first six cards were clicked and 32 resolve correctly.

**One scroll region.** `.pages` 900/900 (a dead reserved bar) + `.page-catalog-pages` 900/9,640 (a live inset one) → `.pages` 900/5,718 and nothing nested, at 900, 1440 and 3440 — the same single scroller every other page on the site uses. Cause was three files each right on its own: the day page only sits in a catalog because `ai/page.js` calls `catalog()`, and `ai.css` had already hidden that catalog’s rail. One nested block in `ai.css` releases the bounded split; `Page.css` and `catalog.css` untouched.

**`public/styles.css:97` — Mike’s "0 space between the viewport top and the date header".** `.page.topic` opted out of page padding with `--page-pad: 0`, and that token **inherits** — so every `.page` under `/framework/` resolved `padding: var(--page-pad, var(--pad-y) 0)` to `0` and `--pad-y: 3em` never fired, sitewide. Now `padding: 0` on the shell itself. **Every framework page just gained ~46px top and bottom** — concurrent measuring baselines moved.

![the day page at 1440](/framework/ai/2026-08-17/day-page-ux/after-1440.png)

**Deleted** (each failed "is it a link or a number?"): the 12-line `day.jsonl` header strip → a fold at the foot, on `wide`, 111 lines, every one an `<a>` to its task · `card.js`’s `t.m.tab` (the VS Code window title, on all 30 cards) · a running card’s dispatch `request` (52px × 4 live tasks, and the whole reason `LANDED` sat below the fold) · two of three lines of intro prose · `ai.css`’s `.page > .ai-dashboard { grid-column: wide }`, the fourth and last copy of the `bleed` payback rule.

**What the model says now**, `ux-v1` @1440 — purpose: before *"a daily AI work-log page … so a reviewer can triage"*, after *"a daily AI task dashboard — it shows Mike which AI jobs are actively running right now"*. `card-ux-v1` (written from the field inventory) found the same defect from a whole page and from one cropped card — the title had no link treatment while the pills looked clickable. Fixed, plus `running 1h 43m` for a clock time and a disclosure triangle on the fold.

**Left:** the rail still builds 158 hidden `.ai-card`s on every day and task page (`display: none`, so nobody sees the work) · the two-column card-as-nav state does not exist — `ai-board-fix` removed it deliberately, so `task-1440.png`/`task-3440.png` show one column · `vision-pilot`’s `?run=` pill is the 1 bad link of 33 · `run.mjs`’s region picker spent 2 of 4 region shots on `div.sidebar` (wants a `--sel` flag) · the date `h1` still leads the page, which every model read still flags.
